title: SQL
summary: Consolidates SQL as a standard, declarative relational language and surveys definition, querying, reusable database objects, security, and application use.

concepts.title: SQL as a standard language
concepts.summary: SQL is a standardized, declarative language used to define, query, maintain, and control relational data across database products.

concepts.title: Set-oriented processing
concepts.summary: SQL states the desired relational result and operates on sets of rows rather than requiring record-by-record navigation.

sections.title: Creating a table and data types

concepts.title: Data definition
concepts.summary: CREATE TABLE specifies columns, data types, keys, nullability, and other constraints that define a relation.

concepts.title: Choosing data types
concepts.summary: Character, numeric, temporal, Boolean, and large-object types should be chosen to match the values and operations a column requires.

concepts.title: Collation
concepts.summary: Collation rules determine how character values are compared and ordered for a language or locale.

concepts.title: Scalar functions
concepts.summary: Scalar functions transform one value per evaluated row, including text, numeric, and date-time values.

concepts.title: Aggregate functions
concepts.summary: Aggregate functions summarize sets or groups of rows, with grouping and filtering rules controlling the scope.

concepts.title: Views
concepts.summary: A view is a named virtual table derived from a query and can simplify or constrain access to underlying tables.

concepts.title: Indexes
concepts.summary: An index stores an ordered access structure that can speed retrieval and may also enforce uniqueness when defined that way.

concepts.title: Database catalog
concepts.summary: The catalog exposes metadata about database objects such as tables and columns for administrative queries.

concepts.title: GRANT and REVOKE
concepts.summary: GRANT assigns specific object privileges to a principal and REVOKE removes previously assigned privileges.

concepts.title: Interactive and embedded SQL
concepts.summary: SQL can be used interactively or embedded within a procedural program whose control flow handles row-by-row application processing.
